hints: Think about the unit form of every separate term, not only the two sides as wholes.
Separate what the check can reject from what it cannot prove.

walkthrough.text: Reduce each side and each term joined by addition or subtraction to SI base units.
The equation is homogeneous only if all those complete unit forms match.
A match shows that the equation is unit-consistent, but physical reasoning and evidence are still needed to establish whether the model is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: States that both sides and every additive or subtractive term must reduce to the same SI base-unit form
States that passing a homogeneity check does not prove that the physical equation is correct

evidence.role: The mapped leaves ground unpredictable reading-to-reading variation and scatter; the steady-quantity scenario and options are original

hints: Ask whether the readings share one direction or change direction unpredictably.
Do not confuse a pattern in measurements with a unit check on an equation.

walkthrough.text: The readings lie on both sides of a central value, so there is no fixed direction to the changes.
That pattern is unpredictable variation between repeated measurements.
This is random error, so option B is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects random error because the readings vary unpredictably with no fixed direction

evidence.role: The mapped leaves ground zero offset as an apparatus-specific systematic fault; the balance values and correction are original

hints: The empty balance already reads above true zero.
Choose an operation that moves the indicated mass downward by the observed zero reading.

walkthrough.text: The empty balance reading is +0.04 g, so every indicated mass is 0.04 g too high.
Subtract the signed zero reading: corrected mass = 7.86 g - 0.04 g.
The corrected mass is 7.82 g, so option A is correct.
The result is lower than the indicated reading, matching the direction expected for a positive zero error.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects 7.82 g by subtracting the positive 0.04 g zero reading from 7.86 g

evidence.role: The mapped leaf grounds repeated readings and averaging as the response to random variation; the option set is original

hints: The useful readings must be independent measurements, not copies of one value.
Look for a process in which variations in opposite directions can partly cancel.

walkthrough.text: Random variation changes unpredictably from one independent reading to the next.
Taking several readings reveals this variation rather than relying on one value.
Calculating the mean allows upward and downward variations to partly cancel, so option B is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects repeated readings and their mean as the suitable response to random variation

evidence.role: The mapped leaves ground suitable wire-diameter measurement, same-direction offsets and repeated sampling; the figure layout and exact procedure prompt are original

hints: Separate the instrument check from the sampling plan.
A representative wire diameter may require both different positions and different orientations.

walkthrough.text: Choose an instrument suitable for the small wire diameter.
Check the reading at true zero before placing the wire between the measuring faces.
Take several corrected readings across positions and orientations, then use their mean to represent the wire.

evidence.role: Directly grounds selection of a suitable instrument for a thin wire diameter

hints: A metre rule cannot separate the small scale markings needed for a thin wire.
Choose an instrument designed for small diameters.

walkthrough.text: The dimension to be measured is the small diameter of a thin wire.
A micrometer screw gauge is designed for this scale of measurement.
A suitable digital micrometer or sufficiently sensitive digital calipers would serve the same measurement role.

ai_rubric.observable: Names a micrometer screw gauge or another suitably sensitive instrument for the thin wire diameter

evidence.role: Grounds a zero or calibration fault that biases every apparatus reading

hints: Create a true zero input before measuring the wire.
Explain whether the non-zero value affects one reading or every reading.

walkthrough.text: Bring the micrometer measuring faces gently together with nothing between them.
The correct reading for this true zero input is zero, so any non-zero display is a zero error.
That signed value is carried into every uncorrected diameter reading, giving a consistent systematic offset.

ai_rubric.observable: Checks the micrometer reading when its measuring faces are gently closed with no wire present
States that a non-zero result gives the same signed systematic offset to all uncorrected diameter readings

evidence.role: Directly grounds repeated readings across wire locations or orientations and calculation of a mean

hints: Think about how the wire may differ along its length and around its cross-section.
State what is done after all signed corrections have been applied.

walkthrough.text: Measure at several separated positions along the wire.
Turn the wire and measure more than one diameter orientation at each position.
Apply the same signed zero correction to every reading.
Calculate the mean of the corrected readings so the result represents the sampled wire and reduces the effect of random variation.

ai_rubric.observable: Takes repeated diameter readings at several positions and in different orientations around the wire
Applies any zero correction and calculates the mean of the corrected readings

evidence.role: The mapped leaves ground contrasting systematic offset and random scatter; the five-reading balance dataset and arithmetic are original

hints: Keep the mean calculation and signed zero correction as separate stages.
Use the direction of the empty reading to check the direction of the final correction.

walkthrough.text: Classify the empty reading from its true-zero condition and its shared effect.
Calculate the mean of all five indicated sample values.
Subtract the positive zero reading, then explain why this correction has a different job from averaging.

evidence.role: Grounds an instrument zero fault as a same-direction systematic error

hints: The input is truly zero when the balance is empty.
Track the sign of the displayed value into later readings.

walkthrough.text: An empty balance has a true input of zero but displays +0.06 g, so this is a positive zero error.
The same +0.06 g is added to each uncorrected indicated mass.
A shared upward offset is systematic because it acts consistently in one direction.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies the +0.06 g empty reading as a positive zero error
Explains that it is systematic because the same upward offset affects every uncorrected sample reading

evidence.role: Grounds processing repeated readings separately from correction of a shared systematic effect

hints: Add all five indicated masses before dividing by five.
A positive zero value has made the display too high.

walkthrough.text: Divide by five: mean indicated reading = 92.24 g / 5 = 18.448 g, or 18.45 g to the display scale.
Subtract the positive zero reading: corrected mean = 18.448 g - 0.06 g = 18.388 g.
Report 18.39 g to the display scale. The corrected result is lower, as required for a positive zero error.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the mean indicated reading as 18.448 g, or 18.45 g when rounded to the display scale
Subtracts the positive 0.06 g zero reading to obtain 18.388 g, or 18.39 g when rounded

evidence.role: Directly grounds the different effects of systematic and random errors on repeated measurements

hints: Ask which changes can occur in opposite directions.
Ask what happens when the same +0.06 g is included in every term of a mean.

walkthrough.text: The five indicated readings vary above and below their own mean, so the variable contributions can partly cancel in an average.
Every reading also contains the same +0.06 g zero offset.
The mean of values that each contain +0.06 g still contains +0.06 g, so averaging cannot remove it.
The repeat-and-mean step addresses random variation, while the signed subtraction addresses the systematic zero error.

ai_rubric.observable: Explains that upward and downward random variations partly cancel when repeated readings are averaged
Explains that averaging preserves the shared +0.06 g zero offset, so a separate signed correction remains necessary

evidence.role: The mapped leaves ground systematic offset, random scatter and averaging. The supplied R = L/t card activates the verified earlier-module homogeneity handoff without teaching later-topic physics.

hints: Keep the unit check, mean and zero correction as separate stages.
Use the sign of the zero check to predict whether the corrected time is higher or lower.

walkthrough.text: Test the supplied model using only the stated units from the earlier module.
Calculate the mean of the five indicated times.
Apply the signed zero correction, then match each feature of the data to its own remedy.

evidence.role: Dependency application is grounded in the verified 9702_t01_cm02 handoff; no later-topic model demand is claimed

hints: Replace length by m and time by s.
Compare the simplified right-hand unit directly with the stated unit of R.

walkthrough.text: The right-hand unit is [L/t] = m/s.
Write this in SI base-unit power form as m s^-1.
The stated left-hand unit [R] is also m s^-1, so the supplied model is homogeneous.

ai_rubric.observable: Simplifies the unit of L/t to m s^-1
Concludes that R = L/t is homogeneous because both sides have unit m s^-1

evidence.role: Grounds repeated-reading processing and a separate same-direction correction; the dataset is original

hints: The five readings have been chosen so their sum can be checked exactly.
A positive zero reading makes every indicated time too high.

walkthrough.text: Add the five indicated times: 0.204 + 0.202 + 0.206 + 0.203 + 0.205 = 1.020 s.
Divide by five: mean indicated time = 1.020 s / 5 = 0.204 s.
Subtract the signed positive zero reading: corrected mean = 0.204 s - 0.004 s = 0.200 s.
The corrected mean is lower than the indicated mean, independently confirming the correction direction.

ai_rubric.observable: Adds the five indicated times and divides by five
Obtains the mean indicated time of 0.204 s
Subtracts the positive 0.004 s zero reading to obtain a corrected mean time of 0.200 s

evidence.role: Grounds contrasting a shared systematic offset with unpredictable variation between repeated readings

hints: One feature changes from reading to reading.
The other feature is measured directly before the event trials and has one fixed sign.

walkthrough.text: The five times differ from one another above and below their mean, which is random variation.
Averaging lets variations in opposite directions partly cancel.
The zero check is +0.004 s every time, so it is a consistent systematic offset.
Because a shared offset cannot cancel in a mean, it requires the separate signed subtraction.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies the reading-to-reading scatter as random variation and explains that averaging allows opposite variations to partly cancel
Identifies the +0.004 s zero reading as a consistent systematic offset requiring a separate signed correction
